missions.title: Blood on King Street
missions.weather: night, snow and ice underfoot, first-quarter moonlight
missions.summary: The Boston Massacre as the game's opening: cutscene built strictly from Rex v. Preston trial testimony, then a playable aftermath carrying a wounded neighbor home through a city on the edge of eruption.

objectives.text: Reach the Royal Exchange Lane surgeon's rooms without being caught in the crowd surges

missions.title: The Gaspee
missions.location: Namquid Point, Narragansett Bay, Rhode Island
missions.weather: moonless night, calm water, low tide
missions.summary: Night longboat raid on the grounded revenue schooner HMS Gaspee. Historical constraint honored as mechanics: Lt. Dudingston is wounded but no one is killed, the crew is put ashore, the ship burns to the waterline.

objectives.text: Board the Gaspee before the tide refloats her
No killing — the raiders took the crew off alive
Keep every raider unidentified (the Crown's inquiry never named them)

missions.title: Saltwater Tea
missions.summary: The Tea Party as a discipline mission: destroy 342 chests of East India Company tea, harm no one, damage nothing else, steal nothing. A participant who pocketed tea was historically stripped and shamed — pilfering is a fail state.

objectives.text: Break and dump every chest before the Royal Navy reacts
No violence, no theft, no damage beyond the tea — replace the broken padlock
Sweep the decks clean before leaving (the crews did)

missions.title: The Powder Alarm
missions.summary: Gage's troops seize provincial powder from the Quarry Hill magazine; rumor inflates it into open war. Ride to raise your town's company — and meet the men whose names will fill your muster roll for the next fourteen years.

objectives.text: Alert and assemble your militia company on the town common
Separate rumor from fact along the way — false alarm spread costs standing

missions.title: Leslie's Standoff
missions.summary: Col. Leslie's 64th Foot comes for hidden cannon; the drawbridge is up and the town gathers. A standoff won with nerve and negotiation, not fire — hold the line without a shot. The war almost begins seven weeks early; it doesn't.

objectives.text: Keep the militia steady — cohesion above waver — while negotiation plays out
Zero shots fired: any discharge fails the mission

missions.title: Nineteenth of April
missions.location: Lexington Green — North Bridge, Concord — the Battle Road
missions.weather: clear spring day after a cold night
missions.summary: Triptych. Lexington Green: a scripted tragedy you cannot win, only witness and survive. North Bridge: the first ordered American volley. Battle Road: a running wall-to-wall skirmish harrying the column back to Boston. The full combat tutorial arc.

objectives.text: Green: survive and disperse — do not stand against the volley
North Bridge: hold Present until the order, then fire by division
Battle Road: leapfrog fire positions along the walls; keep your company ahead of the flankers
Bring every man of your own company home

missions.title: The Redoubt
missions.weather: hot, clear; Charlestown burning by afternoon
missions.summary: Act finale. Hold the redoubt through two full British assaults with disciplined volley work at murderous range; when the ammunition gives out on the third, conduct a fighting withdrawal across Charlestown Neck. Peter Salem and Salem Poor stand in the ranks; Dr. Joseph Warren dies covering the retreat. A defeat that proves the army can stand.

objectives.text: Break two assaults — hold fire until the order at fifty yards
Third assault: withdraw by ranks through the sally port, rearguard at the rail fence
Bring off the wounded; every fit man carried one

missions.title: Cambridge Camp
missions.summary: First winter-quarters-style hub (in summer camp form). Washington takes command of the Continental Army on July 3 — your first sight of him. Convert a militia company into something that can become an army: first drill, first enlistment papers, first inventory of everything the army lacks.

objectives.text: Sign your company to Continental enlistments (expiring December 31, 1775 — the clock that will haunt you)
Meet the army: Washington, Knox, Greene introductions
